research_question: How well does a standard CNN classify BreakHis images?
features: 1280-D backbone features (used directly by classifier head)
main_finding: Strong specificity, weaker sensitivity than other approaches
limitation: Overfits after epoch 1; lowest sensitivity of core models

research_question: How well does a frozen general-purpose foundation model classify BreakHis images alone?
main_finding: Best AUPRC among core models; strong general-purpose representation
limitation: Not fine-tuned on domain data; validation AUROC did not fully transfer to test

research_question: Does combining CNN and Foundation representations improve over either alone?
model: 1280-D CNN + 384-D DINOv2 -> 256-D projections each -> 512-D concat -> shallow classifier
main_finding: Best AUROC, F1, accuracy, sensitivity among core models
limitation: AUROC gain over individual models is marginal (+0.0025 to +0.0033)

research_question: Does patient/group-aware aggregation of fused representations improve prediction?
model: Gated attention (Ilse et al. style) over per-image 512-D fused vectors, grouped by patient
input: Variable-size set of fused vectors per patient group
aggregation: Attention-weighted average within patient/group (NOT true WSI-MIL)
main_finding: Perfect sensitivity (1.0) and highest F1, but AUROC dropped -- test set only 13 groups
limitation: Statistically inconclusive due to very small test group count (n=13)

research_question: Can combining CNN, Foundation-only, and Fusion predictions with validation-selected weights improve robustness?
model: Weighted average of 3 models' probabilities, weights grid-searched on validation only
main_finding: Collapsed to Foundation-only; no improvement over best individual model
limitation: Ensemble did not add value in this setup; weights were validation-set-specific
